region: Castel di Lama · Ascoli Piceno, Marche, Italy
about: Tenuta De Angelis is a family estate in Castel di Lama, in the province of Ascoli Piceno at the southern tip of the Marche, just north of the Abruzzo border. Vines were first planted here in the 1950s, and the winery is run today by proprietor and winemaker Quinto Fausti with his son Alighiero. Their 45 hectares straddle the regional border, with the main vineyard on the hills of Offida at 280 to 350 meters. Gambero Rosso credits the family’s strict fruit selection for wines that deliver well above their price.

Rosso Piceno is the traditional red of southern Marche, built on Montepulciano and Sangiovese. De Angelis blends about 70 percent Montepulciano with 30 percent Sangiovese from certified organic vineyards on loose clay with an eastern exposure. Fermentation is in stainless steel with native yeasts, and sulfur is held to a low ceiling of 80 milligrams per liter. The wine spends about four months in steel and six in bottle before release, with no time in oak, an approach that keeps the focus on fresh fruit; Gambero Rosso has called it “a consumer’s dream.”
